_what_this_is: The claim states a chip can carry, from build.py STATES. Only 'exists' is the fully-earned one. Two share a CSS class today (spec and partial both use st-s) and render identically — the chip component should give them enough range to stay distinct.

states.label: measured
states.means: Measured by our own pipeline on a named workload and date.

states.label: read, not run
states.means: Read from a published source on this date. Never executed by us.

states.label: projected
states.means: Arithmetic, not an invoice. The workings are shown.

states.label: specified, not built
states.means: A specification. The thing it specifies does not exist yet.

states.label: delivered by a person
states.means: A named security professional does this work and signs it off. It is somebody's time rather than a pipeline, which is why its delivery estimate depends on availability.

states.label: built, not located
states.means: It was built. It has not been found since, and until it is, nothing here promises it.

states.label: a booking, not a download
states.means: What is bought is a person's time, not a file.

states.label: part exists
states.means: One half of it runs. The half that carries the guarantee does not.

states.label: does not exist yet
states.means: It does not exist. It is listed so that nobody proposes it as new.
